content.quick: In reflective measurement models, indicators are manifestations caused by the latent construct (arrows point outward from circle to boxes). In formative models, indicators collectively define and cause the construct (arrows point inward from boxes to circle). Misidentifying measurement direction is a critical methodological error.

sentences.text: The distinction between reflective and formative measurement models is the most critical conceptual foundation in structural equation modeling.
sentences.simple: Knowing whether arrows point out or in between your concepts and questions is the most important rule in SmartPLS.
sentences.plain: The distinction between reflective and formative measurement models is the most critical conceptual foundation in structural equation modeling.
sentences.technical: Correct epistemic specification of auxiliary measurement theories represents an indispensable prerequisite for construct validity in structural equation models.

sentences.text: In a reflective model, all questionnaire items share a common underlying cause and are expected to correlate positively with one another.
sentences.simple: In a reflective construct, all your survey questions measure different angles of the same underlying feeling or idea.

sentences.technical: Reflective measurement posits that item covariance stems exclusively from variation in the unobserved latent variable, yielding highly collinear indicator sets.

questions.q: In SmartPLS 4, which direction do the measurement arrows point for a standard reflective construct?
options: From the indicators (rectangles) to the latent construct (circle)
From the latent construct (circle) to the indicators (rectangles)
No arrows are used in reflective models
questions.explanation: In reflective models (Mode A), the latent variable is assumed to cause the indicators, so arrows point outward from the circle to the rectangles.
